text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Monday.

LONDON - British stocks edged lower, depressed by a weaker Wall Street, after trading in a tight range. The FTSE 100 fell 6.8 points to 4,212.0 after drifting down as the Dow gave up early gains and was off 35 points as London closed.

FRANKFURT - German shares ended slightly lower, as activity flags ahead of Wall Street opening and key U.S. employment cost data due on Tuesday. The DAX index fell 3.71 points to 2,994.53 points. In after-hours trading the index stood at 2,992.55.
PARIS - French shares managed small gains despite weakness on Wall Street. The blue-chip CAC-40 index rose 4.83 points to 2,435.17.

ZURICH - Swiss shares rose but gave up bigger gains as a bout of late profit-taking kicked in, triggered by weakness in U.S. trading. The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) rose 2.96 points to 2,642.51.

TOKYO - Japanese stocks fell again, with the key market index falling 2 percent. Brokers said overall sentiment was hurt by reignited fears over bank profits. The key 225-share Nikkei average fell 354.46 points to 17,334.90.
HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks registered their fifth consecutive losing session, succumbing to concerns about interest rates and weak U.S. markets. The Hang Seng Index fell 84.65 points to 13,294.90.
SYDNEY - The Australian stock market was closed for a public holiday.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended little changed. The overall index rose 4.7 points to 6,689.3, the industrial index added 1.1 points to 8,043.9 and the gold index was up 4.9 points to 1,375.3.
